item.title: Kishimen and Nagoya's Noodle Traditions — Guide
item.description: Kishimen are Nagoya’s signature noodles: broad, flat and silky ribbons that slip through a delicate broth tinted with the region’s tamari soy sauce, topped simply with fried tofu, spinach, bonito flakes and a swirl of green onion. The dish’s most beloved settings are its least formal — the standing noodle counters on Nagoya Station’s platforms, where travellers slurp a bowl between trains, and the venerable shop inside Atsuta Jingu’s forest — while the city’s other noodle monument, miso nikomi udon, simmers firm udon directly in a scalding hatcho-miso broth in individual clay pots, the two dishes bracketing Nagoya’s noodle culture from delicate to mighty.
